paragraphs: Centrus Energy Corp., a Delaware corporation, is a trusted supplier of nuclear fuel components for the nuclear power industry, which provides a reliable source of carbon-free energy, and provides enrichment and technical services for public and private customers. References to "Centrus", the "Company", "our", or "we" include Centrus Energy Corp. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries as well as the predecessor to Centrus, unless the context indicates otherwise.

Centrus operates two business segments: (a) LEU, which supplies various components of nuclear fuel to commercial customers from our global network of suppliers, and (b) Technical Solutions, which provides advanced uranium enrichment for the nuclear industry and the U.S. government and advanced manufacturing and other technical services to government and private sector customers. Our current uranium enrichment involves HALEU production and other capabilities necessary for production of advanced nuclear fuel to power existing and next-generation reactors around the world.

Our LEU segment provides most of the Company's revenue and involves the sale of LEU, the fissile component of nuclear fuel, primarily to utilities that operate commercial nuclear power plants. The majority of these sales are for the enrichment component of LEU, which is measured in SWU. Centrus also sells natural uranium hexafluoride (the raw material needed to produce LEU) and occasionally sells uranium concentrates, uranium conversion, or LEU with the natural uranium hexafluoride and SWU components combined into one sale.

LEU is a critical component in the production of nuclear fuel for reactors that produce electricity. We supply LEU and its components to both domestic and international utilities for use in nuclear reactors worldwide. We provide LEU from multiple sources, including medium- and long-term supply contracts, spot purchases and our inventory. As a long-term supplier of LEU to our customers, our objective is to provide value through the reliability and diversity of our supply sources.

Our LEU segment backlog includes medium and long-term sales contracts and contingent sales commitments with major utilities through 2040. We have secured cost-competitive supplies of SWU under long-term contracts through the end of this decade designed to allow us to fill our existing customer orders and make new sales. However, supply chain disruptions may impact our ability to fill existing customer orders. A market-related price reset provision in the TENEX Supply Contract, which is our largest supply contract, became effective in 2019 – when market prices for SWU were near historic lows – which has significantly lowered our cost of sales and contributed to improved margins since 2019.

Our Technical Solutions segment is focused on uranium enrichment for the nuclear industry and the U.S. government and advanced manufacturing, engineering and other technical services to government and private sector customers. Under a contract with the DOE, our Technical Solutions segment is operating uranium enrichment capacity for HALEU production, and other capabilities necessary for production of advanced nuclear fuel to meet the evolving needs of the global nuclear industry and the U.S. government. We are also leveraging our unique technical expertise, operational experience, and specialized facilities to expand and diversify our business beyond uranium enrichment, offering new services to existing and new customers in complementary markets.

Our Technical Solutions segment is committed to the restoration of America's domestic uranium enrichment capabilities for LEU and HALEU, in order to play a critical role in meeting U.S. national security and energy security requirements and advancing America's clean energy, energy security, and national security objectives. Our Technical Solutions segment is also focused on repairing broken and vulnerable supply chains, providing clean energy jobs, and supporting the communities in which we operate. Our goal is to deliver major components of the next-generation nuclear fuels that will provide reliable carbon-free power around the world.

The United States has not had domestic uranium enrichment capability suitable to meet U.S. national security requirements since the Paducah GDP shut down in 2013. DOE continues to draw down its finite stockpile of Cold War-era enriched uranium but is expected to need a new source of U.S.-origin enrichment in the future. Longstanding U.S. policy and binding nonproliferation agreements prohibit the use of foreign-origin civilian enrichment technology for U.S. national security missions. Our AC100M centrifuge currently is the only deployment-ready U.S. uranium enrichment technology that can meet these national security requirements.

Centrus is pioneering U.S. production of HALEU, enabling the deployment of a new generation of HALEU-fueled reactors to meet the world's growing need for carbon-free power. On October 11, 2023, the Company began enrichment operations at its HALEU production facility in Piketon, Ohio under its contract with DOE. On November 7, 2023, the Company made its first delivery of HALEU to the DOE, completing Phase 1 by successfully demonstrating its HALEU production process. HALEU is a high-performance nuclear fuel component that will be required by a number of advanced reactor and fuel designs that are now under development for commercial and government uses. While existing reactors typically operate on LEU with the U235 concentration below 5%, HALEU is further enriched so that the U235 concentration is between 5% and 20%. The higher U235 concentration offers a number of potential advantages, which may include better fuel utilization, improved performance, fewer refueling outages, simpler reactor designs, reduced waste volumes, and greater nonproliferation resistance.

The lack of HALEU supply is a major obstacle to the successful commercialization of these new reactors. For example, in surveys of advanced reactor developers conducted by the U.S. Nuclear Industry Council in 2020 and 2021, respondents indicated that the number one issue that "keeps you up at night" was access to HALEU. As the only company with a license from the NRC actively enriching up to 20% U235 assay HALEU and that is operating a small scaled HALEU production facility, Centrus is uniquely positioned to fill a critical gap in the supply chain and facilitate the deployment of these promising next-generation reactors.

The war in Ukraine, along with the Import Ban Act and the Russian Decree, have contributed to a significant increase in market prices for enrichment and have prompted calls for public and private investment in new, domestic uranium enrichment capacity not only for HALEU production but also for LEU production to support the existing fleet of reactors. As a result, Centrus is exploring the opportunity to deploy LEU enrichment alongside HALEU enrichment to meet a range of commercial and U.S. government requirements, which would bring cost synergies while increasing revenue opportunities. On September 25, 2025, we announced plans for a major expansion of our uranium enrichment capacity in Piketon, Ohio, including plans for large-scale production of both LEU and HALEU. In December 2025, we initiated design work on a 150,000 square foot training, operations and maintenance Facility in Piketon, Ohio and began domestic centrifuge manufacturing to support commercial LEU enrichment activities at our Piketon, Ohio, facility. Our ability to deploy LEU and/or HALEU enrichment, and the timing, sequencing, and scale of those capabilities, is subject to our continued ability to obtain public and private funding.

The Company's work on HALEU began under the HALEU Demonstration Contract executed with the DOE in 2019, to construct a cascade of 16 AC100M centrifuges in Piketon, Ohio to demonstrate HALEU production. The DOE funded the HALEU Demonstration Contract up to $173.0 million with a period of performance that ended November 30, 2022. On November 10, 2022, the DOE awarded the HALEU Operation Contract to the Company with a base contract value of approximately $150.0 million in two phases through 2024. Phase 1 included an approximately $30.0 million cost-share contribution from Centrus matched by approximately $30.0 million from the DOE to complete construction of the cascade, begin operations and produce the initial 20 kilograms of HALEU UF6. On November 7, 2023, the Company made its first contractual delivery of HALEU to the DOE, completing Phase 1 of the contract.

The Company transitioned to Phase 2 of the HALEU Operation Contract in November 2023 which included continued operations and maintenance of the cascade and production for a full year at an annual production rate of 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6. Under Phase 2, Centrus produced and contractually delivered the Phase 2 production target of 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6 to DOE, and was compensated on a cost-plus-incentive-fee basis, with an initial Phase 2 contract value of approximately $90.0 million. As of December 31, 2025, DOE has increased the Phase 2 contract value and related funding to $170.1 million and extended the Phase 2 period of performance to January 31, 2026.

On June 17, 2025, the DOE amended the HALEU Operation Contract to divide the first three-year option period into a first option period of one year ("Option 1a") and a second option period of two years ("Option 1b"). The amendment established a target cost and fee for Option 1a of approximately $99.3 million and $8.7 million, respectively, and a target cost and fee for Option 1b of $163.5 million and $15.2 million, respectively. The DOE exercised Option 1a and extended the period of performance to June 30, 2026. As of December 31, 2025, Option 1a is funded for the contract value of $108.2 million. Additionally, the amendment acknowledged that the estimated cost associated with Option 1b is insufficient to support full performance due to known cost increases since the award of the HALEU Operation Contract and indicated that the Company will need to submit a revised cost proposal for review and negotiation prior to DOE's consideration of Option 1b.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with, and is qualified in its entirety by reference to, the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this report.

This discussion contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results could differ significantly from the results discussed in the forward-looking statements particularly in light of the economic, social and market uncertainty created by, among other things, the war in Ukraine. See "Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Centrus Energy Corp., a Delaware corporation, is a trusted supplier of nuclear fuel components for the nuclear power industry, which provides a reliable source of carbon-free energy and provides enrichment and technical services for public and private customers. References to "Centrus", the "Company", "our", or "we" include Centrus Energy Corp. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries as well as the predecessor to Centrus, unless the context indicates otherwise.

Centrus operates two business segments: (a) LEU, which supplies various components of nuclear fuel to commercial customers from our global network of suppliers, and (b) Technical Solutions, which provides advanced uranium enrichment for the nuclear industry and the U.S. government and advanced manufacturing and other technical services to government and private sector customers.

Published spot price indicators for SWU reached historic highs in April 2009 at $163 per SWU. In the years following the 2011 Fukushima accident in Japan, spot prices declined more than 75%, bottoming out in August 2018 at $34 per SWU. This was followed by a period of price increases, which reached $195 per SWU by December 31, 2024. In 2025, spot prices continued to increase, reaching $200 per SWU by December 31, 2025, which surpasses the previous historic high. This represents an increase of 3% since the beginning of the year and 488% over the 2018 historic low. This surge in the SWU spot price beginning in 2022 has been driven primarily by uncertainty created as a result of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, coupled with growing interest in nuclear power as a source of secure and carbon-free energy. The contemplation of the imposition of tariffs on LEU, if ultimately imposed, may put additional upward pressure on the price of SWU. For further details, refer to Part I, Item 1A, Risk Factors - The current war in Ukraine and related international or U.S. sanctions, tariffs and restrictions on trade, and the Russian response thereto, could have a material adverse impact on our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

When Russian supply is included, the uranium enrichment segment of the global nuclear fuel market is oversupplied, but without Russian supply, the global market for uranium enrichment would be undersupplied. Further, it is not clear that there are sufficient inventories of enriched uranium in the United States to compensate for a loss of Russian supply, absent new capacity that will take a number of years to deploy.

Changes in the supply-demand balance and in the competitive landscape arising from the war in Ukraine or the imposition of tariffs may affect pricing trends, change customer spending patterns, and create uncertainty in the uranium market. At the same time, uncertainty remains about future demand for nuclear power generation. To address such changes and uncertainty, we continue to evaluate opportunities to grow our business organically or through acquisitions and other strategic transactions.

The Company's work on HALEU began under the HALEU Demonstration Contract, executed with the DOE in 2019, to construct a cascade of 16 AC100M centrifuges in Piketon, Ohio to demonstrate HALEU production. The DOE has funded the HALEU Demonstration Contract up to $173.0 million with a period of performance that ended November 30, 2022.

On November 10, 2022, the DOE awarded the HALEU Operation Contract to the Company with a base contract value of approximately $150.0 million in two phases through 2024. Phase 1 included an approximately $30.0 million cost-share contribution from Centrus matched by approximately $30.0 million from the DOE to complete construction of the cascade, begin operations and produce the initial 20 kilograms of HALEU UF6. On November 7, 2023, the Company made its first contractual delivery of HALEU to the DOE, completing Phase 1 of the HALEU Operation Contract.

During November 2023, the Company transitioned to Phase 2 of the HALEU Operation Contract, which included production of 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6 for one production year, as well as continued operations and maintenance of the cascade. Phase 2 included an initial contract value of approximately $90.0 million and compensation on a cost-plus-incentive-fee-basis. The DOE owns the HALEU produced from the demonstration cascade. The HALEU Operation Contract also gives DOE the ability to exercise three optional periods to contract for up to nine additional years of production from the cascade beyond the base contract; those options are at the DOE's sole discretion and subject to the availability of Congressional appropriations. Pursuant to an amendment to the Company's lease for the Piketon facility, the DOE assumed all D&D liabilities arising out of the HALEU Operation Contract.

Under the HALEU Operation Contract, DOE is contractually obligated to provide the 5B Cylinders necessary to collect the output of the cascade, but supply chain challenges created difficulties for DOE in securing enough 5B Cylinders for the entire Phase 2 production year. During time periods when 5B Cylinders were insufficient, the Company was not able to produce HALEU as it did not have 5B Cylinders to store the enriched uranium. Due to these delays, Centrus was unable to achieve contractual delivery of the 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6 by November 2024, which was the date set for the end of Phase 2 performance. On November 5, 2024, the HALEU Operation Contract was modified to extend the Phase 2 period of performance to June 30, 2025, which allowed the Company to produce and contractually deliver the Phase 2 production target of 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6 to DOE. The DOE further extended the Phase 2 period of performance through January 31, 2026, to allow the Company to complete outstanding change orders. As of December 31, 2025, the total Phase 2 contract value and funded value is $170.1 million. The fee for the Phase 2 period of performance that was extended beyond November 30, 2024 was not definitized and is subject to negotiation.

On June 17, 2025, the DOE amended the HALEU Operation Contract to divide the first three-year option period into a first option period of one year ("Option 1a") and a second option period of two years ("Option 1b"). The amendment established a target cost and fee for Option 1a of approximately $99.3 million and $8.7 million, respectively, and a target cost and fee for Option 1b of $163.5 million and $15.2 million, respectively. The DOE exercised Option 1a and extended the period of performance to June 30, 2026. As of December 31, 2025, Option 1a is funded for the contract value of $108.2 million. Additionally, the amendment acknowledged that the estimated cost associated with Option 1b is insufficient to support full performance due to known cost increases since the award of the HALEU Operation Contract and indicated that the Company will need to submit a revised cost proposal for review and negotiation prior to DOE's consideration of Option 1b.

Under the HALEU Operation Contract, the Company has submitted several change order requests for work being performed on infrastructure, facility repairs, and 5B Cylinders. The additional work is being performed under the DOE contracting officer's approval or contract modifications. On September 28, 2023, the DOE modified the HALEU Operation Contract to incorporate additional scope for infrastructure and facility repairs, and costs associated with 5B Cylinder refurbishment, for an estimated additional contract value of $5.8 million, without a cost-share provision. As of December 31, 2025, DOE was obligated for costs up to the contract value of $8.8 million for the additional scope work. The DOE modified the HALEU Operation Contract and increased funding in January 2026 and is now obligated for costs up to the current contract value of $9.7 million. For further details refer to Part I, Item 1, Business - Technical Solutions - Government Contracting.

The DOE continues to pursue the availability of HALEU for the ARDP and for the advanced reactor market and the availability of domestically enriched uranium in a quantity that would be sufficient to address a supply disruption and gaps in domestic production and enrichment. Congress appropriated a total of approximately $3.4 billion to the DOE to jumpstart U.S. nuclear fuel production, including both LEU and HALEU enrichment. Based on this funding, the DOE issued a series of three RFPs covering HALEU production, HALEU deconversion, and LEU production. In late 2024, the DOE made initial selections under each of the RFPs. Centrus was among the awardees for all three RFPs under IDIQ structures (the HALEU Deconversion Contract, HALEU Production Contract, and the LEU Production Contract.

paragraphs: Centrus Energy Corp., 一間設立於特拉華州的公司，是核能發電產業中受信賴的核燃料零組件供應商，提供可靠的無碳能源來源，並為公眾與私人客戶提供濃縮與技術服務。提及 "Centrus"、"本公司"、"我們" 或 "我們公司" 時，均指 Centrus Energy Corp. 及其全資子公司，以及 Centrus 的前身，除非語境另有說明。
Centrus 運作兩個業務應報告分部：(a) LEU，透過我們全球供應商網路向商業客戶提供各種核燃料零組件，以及 (b) 技術解決方案，提供先進的鈾濃縮服務給核能產業與美國政府，並提供先進製造及其他技術服務給政府與私人部門客戶。我們目前的鈾濃縮業務涉及 HALEU 生產及其他必要的先進核燃料製造能力，以供應現有與下一代反應器在全球發電使用。
我們的 LEU 應報告分部提供本公司絕大部分的營業收入，涉及 LEU 的銷售，即核燃料的裂變性組成部分，主要銷售給經營商業核能發電廠的電力公司。這些銷售中絕大多數為 LEU 的濃縮組成部分，以 SWU 為單位計算。Centrus 也會銷售天然鈾六氟化物（製造 LEU 所需的原料）並偶爾銷售鈾濃縮物、鈾轉換或 LEU，與天然鈾六氟化物及 SWU 組成一筆銷售。
LEU 是製造核能發電反應器核燃料的關鍵零組件。我們向國內與國際電力公司供應 LEU 及其零組件，用於全球核能反應器。我們透過多種來源提供 LEU，包括中長期供應契約、現貨採購及我們的存貨。作為 LEU 的長期供應商，我們的目標是透過供應來源的可靠性和多樣性為客戶提供價值。

我們的 LEU 應報告分部的待履行訂單包含中長期銷售契約與主要電力公司的條件性銷售承諾至 2040 年。我們已透過中長期契約取得具成本競爭力的 SWU 供應至本十年末，以填補現有客戶訂單並進行新銷售。然而，供應鏈中斷可能影響我們履行現有客戶訂單的能力。TENEX 供應契約中的市場相關價格重置條款，於 2019 年生效 – 當時 SWU 市場價格接近歷史低點 – 顯著降低我們的銷售成本，並自 2019 年起改善毛利率。

我們的技術解決方案應報告分部專注於核能產業與美國政府的鈾濃縮，以及為政府與私人部門客戶提供先進製造、工程及其他技術服務。根據與美國能源部（DOE）的契約，我們的技術解決方案應報告分部正在運作 HALEU 生產所需的鈾濃縮能力，以及其他必要的先進核燃料製造能力，以符合全球核能產業與美國政府的未來需求。我們也運用我們獨特的技術專業知識、運營經驗與專門設施，拓展並多元化我們的業務，提供新服務給現有與新客戶，以符合相關產業市場。
我們的技術解決方案應報告分部致力於恢復美國本土的鈾濃縮能力，用於 LEU 與 HALEU，以在美國國防安全與能源安全需求中發揮關鍵角色，並促進美國的潔淨能源、能源安全與國防安全目標。我們的技術解決方案應報告分部也專注於修復破損且脆弱的供應鏈，提供潔淨能源工作機會，並支持我們運營所在地的社區。我們的目標是交付下一代核能燃料的主要零組件，以在全球提供可靠的無碳電力。
美國自 2013 年 Paducah GDP 停運後，已無符合美國國防安全需求的本土鈾濃縮能力。能源部（DOE）持續消耗其有限的冷戰時期鈾濃縮存量，但預期未來將需要新的美國原產地濃縮來源。長期美國政策與具有法律約束力的防擴散協議禁止使用外國原產地民用濃縮技術用於美國國防安全任務。我們的 AC100M 離心機目前是唯一可部署的美國鈾濃縮技術，可符合這些國防安全需求。

Centrus 正在美國推動HALEU的生產，使新一代HALEU燃料反應爐得以部署，以應對全球對無碳電力日益增長的需求。2023年10月11日，本公司於俄亥俄州皮克頓的HALEU生產設施開始進行濃縮作業，根據與美國能源部（DOE）的契約。2023年11月7日，本公司首次向DOE交付HALEU，成功完成第一階段，並證明其HALEU生產流程。HALEU是一種高性能核燃料零組件，將被許多正在開發用於商業與政府用途的先進反應爐與燃料設計所需求。雖然現有反應爐通常使用LEU，其U235濃度低於5%，HALEU則進一步濃縮，使其U235濃度介於5%至20%之間。較高的U235濃度可能帶來多種潛在優勢，包括更好的燃料利用率、改善的性能、較少的換料停機時間、簡化的反應爐設計、減少的廢料體積，以及更高的防擴散抗性。
HALEU供應不足是這些新反應爐成功商業化的主要障礙。例如，在美國核能產業協會於2020年和2021年對先進反應爐開發者的調查中，回應者表示，讓他們夜不能寐的首要問題是取得HALEU。作為唯一擁有NRC許可、正在濃縮至20% U235 assay HALEU，且運作小型規模HALEU生產設施的公司，Centrus 能夠填補供應鏈中的關鍵缺口，並促進這些有前景的下一代反應爐的部署。

烏克蘭戰爭，加上進口禁令法案與俄羅斯法令，已導致濃縮市場價格顯著上升，並促使公私部門投資新的國內鈾濃縮能力，不僅用於HALEU生產，也用於LEU生產，以支持現有反應爐隊伍。因此，Centrus 正在探討同時部署LEU與HALEU濃縮的機會，以滿足多樣化的商業與美國政府需求，這將帶來成本協同效益，同時增加收入機會。2025年9月25日，我們宣佈在俄亥俄州皮克頓擴充鈾濃縮能力的計畫，包括大規模生產LEU與HALEU的計畫。2025年12月，我們在俄亥俄州皮克頓展開一個150,000平方英尺的培訓、運作與維護設施的設計工作，並開始進行國內離心機製造，以支持我們在俄亥俄州皮克頓設施的商業LEU濃縮活動。本公司部署LEU與/或HALEU濃縮的能力，以及這些能力的時間、順序與規模，取決於我們持續取得公私部門資金的能力。

本公司於2019年與美國能源部（DOE）簽訂HALEU示範契約，開始進行HALEU相關工作，內容為在俄亥俄州皮克頓建設16部AC100M離心機串聯，用以示範HALEU生產。美國能源部為HALEU示範契約提供資金，總計達173.0 百萬美元，執行期間至2022年11月30日為止。2022年11月10日，美國能源部將HALEU運作契約授予本公司，契約基礎價值約為150.0 百萬美元，分為兩階段執行至2024年。第一階段包含Centrus約30.0 百萬美元的成本分擔，由美國能源部約30.0 百萬美元配合，用以完成離心機串聯建設、開始運作並生產首批20公斤HALEU UF6。2023年11月7日，本公司完成契約第一階段，首次向美國能源部交付HALEU。

本公司於2023年11月轉入HALEU運作契約的第二階段，包括持續運作與維護cascade，並以每年生產900公斤HALEU UF6的速率進行一年的生產。在第二階段，Centrus生產並根據契約向DOE交付了900公斤HALEU UF6的第二階段生產目標，並以成本加 incentive 費用的方式獲得報酬，第二階段契約基礎價值約為90 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，DOE已將第二階段契約價值及相關資金提高至170.1 百萬美元，並將第二階段執行期間延長至2026年1月31日。

2025年6月17日，DOE修改了HALEU運作契約，將第一個三年選項期分為第一選項期為一年（"選項1a"）和第二選項期為兩年（"選項1b"）。此修改設定了選項1a的目標成本與費用約為99.3 百萬美元與8.7 百萬美元，選項1b的目標成本與費用為163.5 百萬美元與15.2 百萬美元。DOE已執行選項1a，並將執行期間延長至2026年6月30日。截至2025年12月31日，選項1a已為契約價值108.2 百萬美元提供資金。此外，此修改承認，由於自HALEU運作契約頒發以來已知的成本增加，與選項1b相關的預估成本不足以支持完全履行，並指出本公司將需要提交修正後的成本提案進行審查與協商，才能讓DOE考慮選項1b。

paragraphs: 以下討論應與本報告中其他地方出現的合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀，並完全以參考這些資料為依據。
本討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論的結果有顯著差異，特別是在烏克蘭戰爭所造成的經濟、社會與市場不確定性等因素的影響下。請參閱本年度報告表10-K開頭的「前瞻性陳述」。
Centrus Energy Corp. 是一家設立於特拉華州的公司，為核能產業提供核燃料零組件，提供可靠的碳中和能源來源，並為公眾與私人客戶提供濃縮與技術服務。文中提及的「Centrus」、「本公司」、「我們」或「我們公司」均指 Centrus Energy Corp. 及其全資子公司，以及 Centrus 的前身，除非文意另有明確說明。
Centrus 運作兩個業務分部：(a) LEU，透過我們全球供應商網路向商業客戶提供各種核燃料零組件，以及 (b) 技術解決方案，為核能產業與美國政府提供先進的鈾濃縮服務，並為政府與私人部門客戶提供先進製造及其他技術服務。

SWU 的公開現貨價格指標在 2009 年 4 月達到歷史高點，為每 SWU 163 美元。在 2011 年日本福島事故後的幾年裡，現貨價格下降超過 75%，至 2018 年 8 月低點為每 SWU 34 美元。此後經歷了一段價格上漲時期，至 2024 年 12 月 31 日達到每 SWU 195 美元。2025 年，現貨價格持續上漲，至 2025 年 12 月 31 日達到每 SWU 200 美元，超過了之前的歷史高點。這代表自年初以來上漲 3%，與 2018 年歷史低點相比上漲 488%。自 2022 年開始的 SWU 現貨價格上漲，主要由俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭所造成的不確定性驅動，同時也伴隨著對核能作為安全且碳中和能源來源的興趣增加。若對 LEU 徵收關稅最終被實施，可能會對 SWU 價格產生額外的上漲壓力。如需進一步細節，請參閱第一部分，項目 1A，風險因素 - 烏克蘭戰爭及相關國際或美國制裁、關稅與貿易限制，以及俄羅斯的回應，可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
當包含俄羅斯供應時，全球核燃料市場的鈾濃縮分部過度供應，但不包含俄羅斯供應時，全球鈾濃縮市場將過度短缺。此外，尚不清楚美國是否有足夠的鈾濃縮存貨，以補償俄羅斯供應的喪失，除非有新的生產能力在數年內投入運作。
由於烏克蘭戰爭或關稅的實施，供應與需求的變化以及競爭格局的改變，可能影響價格趨勢，改變客戶支出模式，並在鈾市場中造成不確定性。同時，未來核能發電需求仍然存在不確定性。為應對這些變化與不確定性，我們持續評估透過內生成長或收購及其他戰略交易來擴大業務的機會。
本公司在 HALEU 方面的工作始於 2019 年與美國能源部（DOE）簽訂的 HALEU 示範契約，用以在俄亥俄州皮克頓建設 16 臺 AC100M 離心機串聯，以示範 HALEU 生產。美國能源部已為 HALEU 示範契約資助至 173.0 百萬美元，執行期間至 2022 年 11 月 30 日為止。

11 月 10 日，2022 年，美國能源部（DOE）將 HALEU 運作契約授予本公司，契約基礎價值約為 150.0 百萬美元，分為兩階段至 2024 年。第一階段包括 Centrus 提供約 30.0 百萬美元的成本分擔，由美國能源部提供約 30.0 百萬美元，以完成 cascade 的建設、開始運作並生產最初的 20 公斤 HALEU UF6。11 月 7 日，2023 年，本公司完成 HALEU 運作契約的第一階段，首次向美國能源部交付 HALEU。

在 2023 年 11 月，本公司轉入 HALEU 運作契約的第二階段，包括生產 900 公斤 HALEU UF6 以供一年生產，以及持續運作與維護 cascade。第二階段的契約基礎價值約為 90.0 百萬美元，並以成本加 incentive 費用的方式進行補償。美國能源部擁有來自示範 cascade 產生的 HALEU。HALEU 運作契約也讓美國能源部有權行使三個選擇性期間，以契約方式延長至最多九年的生產期；這些選擇權由美國能源部單獨決定，並受國會撥款的可用性限制。根據本公司 Piketon 廠區租賃契約的修正案，美國能源部承擔因 HALEU 運作契約產生的所有 D&D 義務。

根據 HALEU 運作契約，美國能源部有義務提供 5B 罐以收集 cascade 的產出，但供應鏈挑戰導致美國能源部在整個第二階段生產年內難以取得足夠的 5B 罐。在 5B 罐不足的期間，本公司無法生產 HALEU，因其沒有 5B 罐來儲存富集鈾。由於這些延誤，Centrus 未能在 2024 年 11 月前完成 900 公斤 HALEU UF6 的契約交付，這是第二階段表現的截止日期。2024 年 11 月 5 日，HALEU 運作契約被修改，將第二階段的表現期間延長至 2025 年 6 月 30 日，使本公司能夠生產並契約交付 900 公斤 HALEU UF6 給美國能源部。美國能源部進一步將第二階段的表現期間延長至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，以讓本公司完成未完成的變更契約。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，第二階段契約價值與已撥款價值總計為 170.1 百萬美元。延長至 2024 年 11 月 30 日後的第二階段表現期間的費用尚未確定，並需經協商。

2025 年 6 月 17 日，美國能源部修改 HALEU 運作契約，將第一個三年選擇性期間分為第一選擇性期間為一年（"Option 1a"）和第二選擇性期間為兩年（"Option 1b"）。修正案設定了 Option 1a 的目標成本和費用約為 99.3 百萬美元和 8.7 百萬美元，以及 Option 1b 的目標成本和費用為 163.5 百萬美元和 15.2 百萬美元。美國能源部行使了 Option 1a，並將表現期間延長至 2026 年 6 月 30 日。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Option 1a 的契約價值為 108.2 百萬美元，已獲得資金支持。此外，修正案承認，與 Option 1b 相關的預估成本因自 HALEU 運作契約頒發以來已知的成本增加，不足以支持完全履行，並指出本公司需提交修正後的成本提案進行審查和協商，才能讓美國能源部考慮 Option 1b。

根據 HALEU 運作契約，本公司已提交多個變更契約請求，用以執行基礎設施、廠區修繕及 5B 罐的相關工作。這些額外工作是在美國能源部契約官員批准或契約修正下進行。2023 年 9 月 28 日，美國能源部修改 HALEU 運作契約，納入基礎設施和廠區修繕的額外範疇，以及與 5B 罐翻新相關的成本，預估額外契約價值為 5.8 百萬美元，不包含成本分擔條款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，美國能源部對額外範疇工作的成本負有責任，最高達契約價值 8.8 百萬美元。美國能源部修改 HALEU 運作契約並於 2026 年 1 月增加資金，現對額外範疇工作的成本負有責任，最高達現行契約價值 9.7 百萬美元。如需進一步細節，請參閱第一部分，項目 1，業務 - 技術解決方案 - 政府契約。

美國能源部持續追求 HALEU 在 ARDP 和先進反應堆市場的可用性，以及足夠數量的國內富集鈾，以應對供應中斷和國內生產與富集的缺口。國會已撥款約 3.4 十億美元給美國能源部，以啟動美國核燃料生產，包括 LEU 和 HALEU 的富集。根據此資金，美國能源部發佈一系列三份 RFP，涵蓋 HALEU 生產、HALEU 去轉換及 LEU 生產。在 2024 年末，美國能源部已對每份 RFP 進行初步選拔。Centrus 是所有三份 RFP 的獲獎者之一，採用 IDIQ 結構（HALEU 去轉換契約、HALEU 生產契約及 LEU 生產契約）。

本公司之業務、財務及營運表現可能因疫情及其他健康相關問題而受到不利影響。
本公司之業務面臨因取得SWU及鈾而產生之價格波動風險。
營運風險
對我們從俄羅斯供應商及其他來源所購買之SWU或鈾之進口或銷售所設立之限制，可能對本公司之獲利能力及業務可行性造成不利影響。
本公司依賴供應商及其他來源之採購以履行對客戶之義務，並依賴第三方提供必要之商品與服務。
關稅及其他國際貿易政策之變動可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司面臨來自主要生產者的激烈競爭，這些生產者可能較不敏感於成本，或因獲得外國政府支持而具優勢。
在某些外國市場中，本公司之競爭能力可能因法律、政治、經濟或其他因素而受到限制。
對我們最大客戶或供應商的依賴可能會對我們造成不利影響。
我們可能無法成功執行在俄亥俄州皮肯頓和田納西州奧克里奇的擴張計畫，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
我們無法保證會獲得任何IDIQ契約下的額外任務契約，且即使獲得契約，任務契約的性質、時間及金額亦存在不確定性。
LEU積壓訂單的金額，如在任一時間點所聲明者，未必能反映未來銷售收入，且存在不確定性。
技術解決方案應報告分部透過各種類型的契約進行業務，包括固定價格契約及成本分擔契約，這會使我們面臨成本超支的風險。
財務風險
我們擁有重大長期負債。
我們0%可轉換票據及2.25%可轉換票據的條件轉換特徵，若被啟動，可能會對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司 0% 可轉換票據及 2.25% 可轉換票據轉換可能稀釋股東持股權益，或可能以其他方式壓低本公司普通股之價格。
0% 可轉換票據及 2.25% 可轉換票據之抵押契約中之某些條款可能延遲或阻止本公司之有益收購嘗試。
償還我們之債務需要大量現金，而我們可能無法從業務中產生足夠之現金流量以償還債務。
本公司之營收及營運結果可能自季度至季度、年度至年度大幅波動，這可能對本公司之現金流量產生不利影響。
若不利條件或情勢變更顯示可能與本公司智慧財產權相關之減損損失，則營運結果可能受到負面影響。
Centrus 依賴 Enrichment Corp. 之內部支援。
本公司 Class A 普通股之少數持有者可能對本公司之經營方向產生重大影響。
本公司利用 NOL 稅額抵減以抵消未來應稅所得之能力可能受到限制。
法律及合規風險
本公司業務受美國政府嚴格規範，包括核能管制委員會（NRC）及能源部（DOE）以及俄亥俄州與田納西州，並可能因政府政策與優先事項的變更而受到重大影響。
paragraphs: 以下討論說明了可能影響我們財務狀況與營運的重要風險因素。這些風險，可能對我們的合併財務報表產生負面影響，主要歸類於下列項目。讀者不應認為任何描述為影響我們的所有潛在風險之完整清單。
•烏克蘭現行戰爭及相關國際制裁與限制；
•因進口禁令法案及俄羅斯法令所導致之市場與供應鏈問題；
•因應烏克蘭入侵事件所實施之政府制裁與關稅，以及由此產生之爭議，我們所遭受之財務損失；
•我們客戶與供應商所經歷之財務困難及其營運狀況；
•疫情及其他健康相關問題；
